name: Utsunomiya

queries.query: Utsunomiya cadastral parcel map official Tochigi registry map GIS land parcel shapefile
queries.result: First-party discovery found Utsunomiya City's official page announcing public cadastral-map data and its official open-data catalog dataset. The city dataset is a citywide Shapefile package with parcel polygons, native fields, and a declared CRS.

queries.query: 宇都宮市 公式 地籍図 地番図 GIS シェープファイル 公図
queries.result: First-party Japanese discovery found the same Utsunomiya City Asset Tax Division publication. It states the map is based on Legal Affairs Bureau public maps and is a tax-assessment reference map, not proof of parcel boundaries, exact position/shape, or rights. The catalog identifies the spatial scope as all Utsunomiya City and the CRS as JGD2011 Japan Plane Rectangular CS IX.

registryBasis: Utsunomiya City itself publishes a citywide parcel-number/cadastral reference dataset and describes its Asset Tax Division as the contact. This is local registry/map evidence, distinct from national-agency prose, but the city limits it to tax-assessment reference use.

officialSources.observation: Official Utsunomiya open-data catalog dataset, titled 地籍図データ, states spatial scope is all Utsunomiya City, temporal extent 2026-01-01, and CRS is JGD2011 / Japan Plane Rectangular CS IX. It provides six parcel-map Shapefile ZIP resources and a field-definition PDF.

Official city page says the data was published in Shapefile form and is based on Legal Affairs Bureau public maps for fixed-asset-tax assessment; it warns the data does not certify parcel boundaries, exact position/shape, or rights.

Ministry of Justice first-party page documents the separate national G-Space publication of registry-office map data. It was recorded as national context only, not as proof of an Utsunomiya-local API.

coverageAssessment.claimedScope: Official catalog says all Utsunomiya City; six split Shapefile resources are published.
coverageAssessment.verifiedOpenScope: One downloaded split around the preserved WUP point was inspected; a bounded native-coordinate query returned six polygon features and three full polygons were retained.

remainingUncertainty: The citywide catalog claim was not independently reconstructed from all six archives. The source is explicitly an assessment/reference map and not a legal cadastral boundary or rights source. No owner, address, titleholder, contact, tax/account or personal fields were requested or retained. Exact-point intersection is not used as a citywide completeness claim.
